run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T23:31:01Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy fired at 2026-11-17T23:31:01Z because frontend-proxy's own 'ingress' spans carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR in nearly every sampled 5-minute window from 23:04:01 onward, peaking at 0.0333 error spans/s at 23:26:01, and the alert's reported value 0.01111111111111111 matches exactly the ingress error-span rate measured at 23:41:01 (0.0111/s) while frontend-proxy still served ~11-12 UNSET spans/s. The dominant 5xx in frontend-proxy's access log is HTTP 503 with response flag UC and detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}, tagged with upstream cluster 'frontend' (observed at 23:00:55 through 23:39:06), i.e. the frontend side terminated connections before a response started; that class predates every change in the window and is the class present around the alert time. A separate, small burst of five HTTP 500 'via_upstream' responses at 23:23:40 coincides with a configuration-only product-catalog Deployment rollout at 23:23:36-23:23:40; the only fault-injection setting switched on in otel-demo is flagd-config's productCatalogFailure ('on', 'Fail product catalog service on a specific product'), which ties to product-catalog, but the declared product-specific failure was not observed and the sustained error signal starts ~19-23 minutes before that rollout, so the flag path remains a hypothesis for the short burst only. Why the frontend terminates connections is unknown: the frontend pod is Running/Ready with CPU throttling of 26-31% under a 100m limit and a working set above its 200Mi limit, which is a candidate, not a verified cause.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's error spans are non-zero in nearly every sampled window: 'ingress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate is 0.0083/s at 23:04:01, 0.0074/s at 23:11:01, 0.0148/s at 23:23:01, 0.0333/s at 23:26:01, 0.0312/s at 23:28:01, 0.0111/s at 23:41:01 and 0.0077/s at 23:44:01, while UNSET ingress spans run at roughly 11-12 spans/s.

At 23:40:00 the instant sums for frontend-proxy were 0.0074 error spans/s versus 20.86 UNSET spans/s; the alert's reported current value 0.01111111111111111 equals the ingress error rate reading of 0.0111/s at 23:41:01, so the alert tracks frontend-proxy ingress error spans.

frontend-proxy's own access log records HTTP 503 with response flag UC and detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on many paths (/api/products/*, /api/cart, /api/data, /api/recommendations, /) with 95-byte responses, at 23:00:55, 23:00:56, 23:04:46, 23:07:48, 23:11:26, 23:12:24, 23:16:34, 23:16:51 (x3), 23:18:39, 23:19:38, 23:21:28, 23:23:36, 23:24:30, 23:29:33, 23:30:04, 23:34:52, 23:38:20 and 23:39:06.

The 503 UC lines name the upstream cluster as 'frontend' (e.g. "GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO ... 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} ... "frontend-proxy:8080" "100.71.221.228:8080" frontend 100.96.3.19:59696 ..."), so the dominant frontend-proxy 5xx are attributed by Envoy to the frontend deployment terminating the connection before a response started.

A distinct burst of five HTTP 500 'via_upstream' responses with 21-byte bodies was logged by frontend-proxy at 23:23:40 for GET /api/products/LS4PSXUNUM, /api/products/2ZYFJ3GM2N, /api/products/HQTGWGPNH4, /api/products/L9ECAV7KIM and POST /api/checkout.

Deployment product-catalog performed a rollout inside the window: ScalingReplicaSet at 23:23:36 (scale up product-catalog-55f64b54c9 0->1) and 23:23:40 (scale down product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc 1->0), ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate product-catalog-55f64b54c9 at 23:23:36, new pod product-catalog-55f64b54c9-lbxd9 Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started 23:23:36-23:23:39, old pod product-catalog-7c7f8b68dc-5spmp Killing at 23:23:40.

The two product-catalog ReplicaSets have identical visible pod-template content: image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-product-catalog and the same env (OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, OTEL_COLLECTOR_NAME, PRODUCT_CATALOG_PORT=8080, PRODUCT_CATALOG_RELOAD_INTERVAL=10, FLAGD_HOST=flagd, FLAGD_PORT=8013, GOMEMLIMIT=16MiB, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES), so a configuration-only change moved the ReplicaSet hash.

The otel-demo/flagd-config ConfigMap holds productCatalogFailure with defaultVariant 'on', state ENABLED and description 'Fail product catalog service on a specific product'; every other fault-injection flag in that file (adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, recommendationCacheFailure) has defaultVariant 'off'.

product-catalog shows no failed spans in the sampled metric data: at 23:45:00 the status breakdown for product-catalog contains only STATUS_CODE_UNSET (~2.97 spans/s), and the per-span STATUS_CODE_ERROR query over frontend, product-catalog and frontend-proxy returned only frontend and frontend-proxy series.

Product pages were served successfully after the product-catalog rollout: frontend-proxy logged repeated 200 responses with 508-byte bodies for GET /api/products/OLJCESPC7Z between 23:39:09 and 23:40:04, and the product-catalog container printed 'Product Found' continuously over 23:39:30-23:40:04.

The frontend's own error spans are confined to a short burst: 'GET' (0.0185/s then 0.0194/s), 'POST', 'POST /api/checkout', 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' and 'tcp.connect' show STATUS_CODE_ERROR only in the samplings at 23:26:01 and 23:28:01, while frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' errors appear only in the same two samplings (0.0222/s, 0.0233/s).

frontend, frontend-proxy and product-catalog pods are Running and Ready with restartCount 0; limits are tight: frontend cpu 100m / memory 200Mi, frontend-proxy cpu 30m / memory 50Mi, product-catalog cpu 15m / memory 30Mi; working set is frontend 239MB->262MB, frontend-proxy ~41MB, product-catalog ~25MB.

CPU throttling ratio over 23:01-23:41 was frontend 0.26-0.31, product-catalog 0.15-0.19 (both old and new pods), frontend-proxy 0.03-0.05, cart 0.20-0.36, ad 0.07-0.34; frontend and product-catalog ratios show no step change after the 23:23:36 rollout.
All five nodes report Ready=True with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure False, so node-level pressure is not observed as a contributor.

The error signal has no pre-window baseline: a 15:51-23:51 query for frontend-proxy ingress by status_code returns its first sample at 23:01:12, with 10-minute UNSET traffic rising from ~1.5 spans/s at 23:01:12 to ~11.7 spans/s at 23:11:12.

The sustained frontend-proxy error signal cannot be attributed to the 23:23:36 product-catalog rollout: 503 UC upstream resets were already logged at 23:00:55/23:00:56 and 23:04:46, and frontend-proxy ingress error spans are non-zero from the 23:04:01 window, roughly 19-23 minutes before the product-catalog pod was replaced.

product-catalog was not observed failing after its rollout: product pages returned 200 to frontend-proxy repeatedly at 23:39:09-23:40:04, product-catalog logged 'Product Found' up to 23:40:04, and product-catalog has no STATUS_CODE_ERROR span series in the window.

Rejected: that the productCatalogFailure flag or its product-catalog rollout is what keeps frontend-proxy's request error rate above zero. The alert-level signal is the 503 UC upstream-reset class, present continuously from 23:00:55, recorded against upstream cluster 'frontend', and unaffected by product-catalog's replacement at 23:23:36; product-catalog produced no error spans and served product pages with 200 afterwards.

Hypothesis: the frontend terminates upstream connections under its own tight runtime constraints - a 100m CPU limit with 26-31% throttled CFS periods throughout the window and a working set above its 200Mi memory limit - for example a Node.js keep-alive/idle-connection close racing with Envoy connection reuse, which would surface as 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} against upstream cluster 'frontend'. Not verified.

Hypothesis: the otel-demo/flagd-config setting productCatalogFailure='on' is the fault injection behind the five 500 responses at 23:23:40, with the configuration-only product-catalog rollout at 23:23:36 as the mechanism by which the value took effect. Unresolved: the declared product-specific failure was not observed afterwards, and no change history shows when the value was set.

Review the RequestErrorRate rule's threshold and 'for' duration: it alerts on an error rate above 0 for a series that is non-zero in most 5-minute windows because of ~0.7% sporadic 503 UC resets; a small non-zero threshold plus a longer 'for' would separate this steady-state noise from a real fault.

Compare the frontend's HTTP server keep-alive/idle-timeout settings with frontend-proxy's Envoy upstream idle timeout, and reconsider the frontend's 100m CPU / 200Mi memory limits, since the upstream connection terminations originate on the frontend side.

Review change history for otel-demo/flagd-config and Deployment product-catalog around 23:23:36 and confirm whether productCatalogFailure is meant to be 'on'; if it is intentional, verify why the product-specific failure is not visible in product-catalog logs or spans.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate rule is not present in the queried Prometheus: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned nothing (no_data view 435c0428-61d8-4770-872b-0a34e1248f71-t1:8eeb7f38-9b54-4a47-93e7-87bee554499e), so its expression, threshold and 'for' duration are unknown.
Change history is not an integrated data source in this Run, so what triggered the product-catalog rollout at 23:23:36 and when flagd-config's productCatalogFailure was switched to 'on' are unknown.

The frontend container log query returned no data (0 lines, 0 bytes for 23:20-23:51; no_data view f59fc294-4957-4ffd-98e7-d4131f6388ae-t1:bea791b5-cbf2-4da2-af18-b4571ab899dd), so the reason the frontend terminates upstream connections cannot be determined.

The product-catalog error-keyword log query returned no data (no_data view 8c71706d-aef2-4250-83c8-fa6a9ff327e8-t1:fd52d0f3-6490-4488-a093-80ae32f1e101); that empty result is only a statement about what that query matched, not proof product-catalog logged no errors.

Jaeger's newest stored traces for frontend-proxy end at about 23:19:31, so no trace-level error spans exist for the 23:23-23:39 error requests; the sampled ingress spans there carry only http.status_code 200/308 with no error details.
Pod log availability ends at about 23:40:05, so the frontend-proxy 5xx pattern between 23:40:05 and 23:51:12 was not observed.

The networkpolicies query for otel-demo returned no data (no_data view 8bea19ea-b099-4326-9f1a-1098d2f37fe6-t1:77f48ba7-63c9-43af-81d3-90f1a6a2799f), so a network-layer contributor cannot be ruled out or confirmed.
Traces tagged http.status_code="500" for frontend-proxy ingress and traces tagged error=true returned no data, so error traces for the affected requests could not be retrieved.
The declared effect of productCatalogFailure (a product-specific failure) was not observed in the sampled logs or spans, so whether that setting is effective at all remains unknown.
next_steps: Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition and its Alertmanager state from the owning Prometheus/Alertmanager instance to confirm the threshold and evaluation window.
Fetch change/audit history for otel-demo/flagd-config and for Deployment product-catalog to identify what changed at 23:23:36 and when productCatalogFailure was set to 'on'.
Capture frontend container stdout/stderr (or enable file logging) while reproducing, to see why Node closes request connections before headers.
Compare frontend-proxy's Envoy upstream idle/keep-alive settings with the frontend server's keep-alive timeout, and test with a larger frontend CPU limit.

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics:
    dimensions:
    - default: otel-demo
      name: namespace
exporters:
  clickhouse:
    endpoint: http://clickhouse-clickhouse.clickhouse.svc.cluster.local:8123
    logs_table_name: otel_demo_logs
    password: ""
    traces_table_name: otel_demo_traces
    username: default
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch-master.opensearch.svc.cluster.local:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel-logs
    logs_index_time_format: yyyy-MM-dd
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector.opentelemetry-collectors.svc.cluster.local:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    endpoint: http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090
    tls:
      insecure: true
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:8889
extensions:
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  resourcedetection:
    detectors:
    - env
    - system
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  nginx:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: http://image-provider:8081/status
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  postgresql:
    endpoint: postgresql:5432
    metrics:
      postgresql.blks_hit:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.blks_read:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.deadlocks:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_deleted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_fetched:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_inserted:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_returned:
        enabled: true
      postgresql.tup_updated:
        enabled: true
    password: [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    tls:
      insecure: true
    username: root
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
    username: valkey
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - debug
      - prometheus
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - nginx
      - otlp
      - postgresql
      - redis
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - clickhouse
      - debug
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resourcedetection
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - pull:
          exporter:
            prometheus:
              host: 0.0.0.0
              port: 8888
